newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel rejects Hapoalim divestiture plan.
newsitem.headline: Israel rejects Hapoalim divestiture plan.

text.p: The Israeli government has rejected a proposal to force Bank Hapoalim to sell its holdings in Koor Industries and Clal Israel, the Treasury said on Wednesday.
"The process of selling control in Bank Hapoalim will continue as planned without undertaking a divestiture of its holding in the Koor and Clal concerns," the Treasury said in a statement.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's economic adviser, Moshe Leon, had suggested the measure last month as an extension of the bank reform legislation implemented last year. The legislation required the banks to reduce their holdings in non-bank companies and for Hapoalim to sell its stake in either Koor or Clal.
Hapoalim, Israel's largest commercial bank, holds 22.7 percent of Koor and 30.9 percent of Clal, two of the biggest holdings companies in the country.

Sources in the prime minister's office said Netanyahu and Finance Minister Dan Meridor agreed at a meeting last night not to seek any further divestitures of Hapoalim. They said legal advisers warned that such a move would be impossible without new and time-consuming legislaton.

The government is seeking to sell a controlling stake in Hapoalim. Newspaper reports in recent weeks have indicated that two groups are forming to compete in a tender, one around U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil and the other around U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur Ted Arison.
"The government's main goal, at the moment, is to complete the sale process of a controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim," the Treasury said.
